content.title: Multimodal contrastive learning traces the early dissemination of Romance of the Three Kingdoms in Thailand
content.abstract: The Romance of the Three Kingdoms (RTK, 三國演義) is a global literary canon, yet how and when it first reached Thailand remains contested because few documents survive. Using the 1838 Wat Prasert Sutthawat murals, the earliest large-scale Thai RTK visual corpus, we build the first expert-verified multimodal dataset for mural–print comparison. We introduce the Mural–Illustration Similarity Prediction (MISP) model, which couples self-supervised multimodal contrastive embedding with supervised cross-modal attention fusion to produce interpretable similarity scores.
